official.deadline_central_display: Varies by programme; the Commission states that in most cases applications run from October to January for courses starting the following academic year
official.deadline_note: There is no single Commission-wide deadline: each master's own website publishes its admission and scholarship deadlines, and the Commission advises applying between October and January for the following academic year.
official.application_cycle: Annual; a new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the catalogue each year
official.status_note: The Commission's student page is live and directs applicants to the current EMJM catalogue and to each consortium's own application portal.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Commission's student page states that 'Masters may also offer full scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide' and that 'Scholarships cover your participation costs and contribute to travel, visa, a living allowance'; it does not itemise tuition, which is set by each consortium.
benefits: Full scholarship to the best-ranked students worldwide
EU scholarship for individuals: EUR 1,400 per month, maximum 24 months
eligibility: Students from all over the world are welcome
Must hold a bachelor's degree (first degree), or be in the last year of bachelor studies
Must graduate before the master's programme starts
A bachelor's equivalent level of learning may be accepted if officially recognised in the degree-awarding country
Applicants apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme
requirements: Apply directly to the institution running the chosen programme via that master's website
Hold a bachelor's degree, or complete it before the programme starts
Meet the entry requirements and follow the application steps published by each consortium, with and without scholarship
documents: Each master's website publishes its own list of required application documents and steps; the Commission does not publish a common document list
selection_criteria: Scholarships are awarded to the best-ranked students worldwide
Ranking and selection are run by the consortium delivering the joint master
coverage: A living allowance of EUR 1,400 per month, for a maximum of 24 months
application_method: Search the EMJM course catalogue for programmes with Polish partners
Open the master's own website for entry requirements, deadlines and application steps
Submit the application directly to the institution running the programme, following its scholarship and non-scholarship routes
official.application_route: Search the Commission's EMJM catalogue, then apply directly to the consortium running the programme - there is no central Commission application.
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction; students from all countries worldwide may apply
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the Commission states students from all over the world are welcome
official.duration: 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits); scholarship paid for a maximum of 24 months
official.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are prestigious international masters, jointly designed and delivered by a group of higher education institutions, involving at least three institutions from at least three different countries, and typically including periods of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence.
official.program_type: EU-funded joint master's degree delivered by an international consortium, with competitive EU scholarships

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a portfolio, not one award: there is no central Commission application, so your real workload is researching each consortium separately and applying to several joint masters with Polish partners in parallel, because a single strong file has a low hit rate. Build your file around the fact that selection is run by the consortium, not Brussels, and that each master sets its own deadline, own language certificate and own document list. The EUR 1,400 monthly figure is a Commission-wide unit cost capped at 24 months, so it does not scale with a longer programme or with a country with higher living costs.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year bachelor's students or recent graduates who can commit to studying in at least two countries and are comfortable running several separate consortium applications in the same October-January window.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist joint masters in the EACEA catalogue that include a Polish university, then bookmark each consortium's own admissions and scholarship page
Build a per-programme deadline tracker for October to January rather than relying on a single closing date
Confirm you will hold your bachelor's degree before the programme starts, and that the diploma is recognisable in the degree-awarding country
Prepare one strong motivation letter skeleton and one CV, then tailor both per consortium instead of writing from scratch each time
Check each consortium's own statement on tuition fees and additional costs, since the Commission's page does not itemise them
common_rejection_risks: Missing a consortium's deadline because you assumed the Commission published one central date
Applying for the scholarship route without meeting the consortium's separate scholarship essay, interview or ranking requirements
Being in your last bachelor's year without a credible graduation date before the master starts
Assuming the EUR 1,400 allowance covers your full budget in whichever two or three countries you will live in
Sending the application to the Commission rather than to the institution running the programme
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa and travel receive only a stated contribution, and tuition is set by each consortium, so installation costs, the gap between the EUR 1,400 allowance and real rents, and any consortium fees remain on you.
document_audit: There is no shared Commission document list - each master's website publishes its own, so check it programme by programme rather than reusing one pack
Degree certificates from outside the EU usually need translation and sometimes legalisation; start early because recognition in the degree-awarding country is a stated condition
Last-year students need documentary proof of expected graduation, not just a statement in the motivation letter
alerts: Only best-ranked applicants get the scholarship, so apply to the non-scholarship route of the same programme as a fallback where the consortium offers one
The Commission's catalogue gains a new batch of selected masters each year, so a programme you found this year may not exist next year and vice versa
An EMJM requires at least three institutions from three different countries, so confirm the mobility route before you accept
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Find the programme in the EACEA catalogue, apply directly to the running institution within its own window, and let the consortium rank you for the scholarship - no Commission-level submission exists.
